title: DPX Mounting of Drosophila CNS
author: Geoffrey W. Meissner
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.qj2duqe
materials: Ethanol and Xylene. All series solutions are replaced (not replenished) based on the number of slides mounted, with monthly replacement generally working well. Replace cloudy solutions immediately.

steps.title: Prepare PLL‑coated cover glasses
steps.instruction: Dip 22 × 22 mm No. 1 cover glasses in cold poly‑L‑lysine (PLL) once (or multiple times) the day before mounting, touching the dripping edge to the PLL jar lip to remove excess; do not touch a Kimwipe. Allow to dry overnight at room temperature in a dust‑ and light‑protected rack. If performing multiple dips, wait at least 1 hour between dips and adjust the number of dips to achieve the desired stickiness.

steps.title: Prepare slide spacers with jig
steps.instruction: Score a 22 × 22 mm No. 2 cover glass down the midline using a diamond cleaver and a glass slide as a straight edge, then snap it into two halves to serve as spacers. Using the slide‑making jig that defines a 1.2 cm central region, place the cut spacers in the cut‑outs so that the factory‑cut edges face the center of the landing strip and the snapped edges face outward. Secure each spacer with tape guided by the jig edge, covering approximately half of the spacer while leaving enough exposed surface for the mounted cover glass to rest solely on the spacers.

steps.title: Second fixation of adult CNS tissue
steps.instruction: Aspirate and discard phosphate‑buffered saline with 0.5 % Triton X‑100 (PBT). Add 1.75 mL of 4 % paraformaldehyde (PFA) in PBS, nutate for 4 hours at room temperature protected from light. After fixation, aspirate and discard the fixative.

steps.title: Wash tissue with PBT (4 × 15 min)
steps.instruction: Add 1.75 mL PBT, nutate 15 minutes at room temperature; repeat for a total of four 15‑minute washes while nutating and protecting from light.

steps.title: Optional storage of fixed tissue
steps.instruction: Store tissue at 4 °C in 2 mL Protein LoBind tubes containing 1.75 mL PBT for up to 3 days; nutate tubes or lay them flat in an empty freezer box on a rotator.

steps.title: Remove detergent with PBS wash
steps.instruction: Aspirate PBT, add ~1.75 mL PBS at room temperature, nutate 10 minutes on a nutator protected from light to wash out detergent.

steps.title: Transfer tissue to T‑dish wells
steps.instruction: Add clean PBS to each well of the T‑dish (do not overfill; each well holds ~120 µL). Transfer the PBS‑washed tissue from the tube to a clean glass dish, then using forceps or a pipette move each sample into a well of the T‑dish, keeping excess solution minimal. The T‑dish grid runs right‑to‑left (6‑5‑4‑3‑2‑1) with row IDs (A‑J) on the right to compensate for the later flip of the cover glass.

steps.title: Place PLL‑coated cover glass in holder
steps.instruction: Insert the prepared PLL‑coated cover glass into the T‑dish cover‑glass holder.

steps.title: Mount brains onto cover glass
steps.instruction: Add a puddle of ~200–500 µL fresh PBS to the region of the cover glass where tissue will be placed, adjusting volume to keep samples submerged and visible. Using forceps, orient each tissue anterior‑up, grasp a safe region (antennal nerves, abdominal nerves, or neck connective), quickly transfer to the mounting area, align with the “T” grid (brain on the horizontal bar, VNC on the vertical bar), and gently lay down without pushing. Rotate the T‑dish rather than the tissue if needed to achieve alignment.

steps.title: Rinse cover glass in MilliQ water
steps.instruction: When all tissues are mounted, remove the cover glass from the holder, dip it in fresh MilliQ water for 2 seconds, briefly touch the edge to the beaker lip to remove excess water, and immediately place it into the first ethanol bath, maintaining tissue‑front and top‑up orientation and handling only the top edge.

steps.title: Ethanol dehydration series
steps.instruction: Sequentially submerge the cover glass (orientation unchanged) in 30 % ethanol for 10 minutes, then 50 % ethanol 10 minutes, 75 % ethanol 10 minutes, 95 % ethanol 10 minutes, followed by three successive 100 % ethanol baths (10 minutes each; the final 100 % bath may be extended to ≥30 minutes if needed). Keep jar front marks facing forward, secure lids tightly, and optionally place a sticky flag on the lid to track progression.

steps.title: Xylene clearing series
steps.instruction: Immediately after the third 100 % ethanol, submerge the cover glass in three successive xylene baths, 5 minutes each, timing precisely with a hood timer; maintain orientation and front‑mark alignment, and keep lids tightly sealed.

steps.title: Prepare DPX dropper and blank slide
steps.instruction: While the xylene baths run, preload a DPX dropper by lifting the tip out of DPX, squeezing the bulb to let DPX run down the bottle wall, keeping the bulb squeezed while submerging the tip back into DPX, then releasing to fill the tip; let the dropper sit for bubbles to rise. Place the slide on the mounting platform in the hood and have a blank slide ready for later pressing.

steps.title: Apply DPX to tissue
steps.instruction: After the final xylene soak, remove the cover glass, hold it horizontally with the tissue side up, and immediately dispense ~7 drops of DPX onto the tissue. Wait ~30 seconds for DPX to self‑level; keep the cover glass level, avoid tilting, and if bubbles appear, use a spare slide or a snapped cotton‑tipped applicator to push them to the edges. Use the pointed end of the applicator, a glass slide, or gloved fingers to add DPX to exposed edges if needed, always preserving tissue‑front/top‑up orientation.

steps.title: Place cover glass onto prepared slide
steps.instruction: Flip the cover glass over so tissue/DPX side contacts the prepared slide, align it centered between the spacers, and gently lower it to avoid trapping air. Let sit ~30 seconds for DPX to spread, then nudge with the edge of a glass slide to center and square it between spacers. Ensure DPX fully surrounds the cover‑glass edges, and gently press the middle with a clean glass‑slide tip without tilting.

steps.title: Cure DPX and dry slide
steps.instruction: Transfer the slide to a drying rack without tilting, cover with a cryo/freezer box lid, and let dry in the hood for a minimum of 24 hours undisturbed. After 24 hours, keep the slide in the hood until DPX is fully cured (~2 days) before imaging. To remove excess cured DPX, gently nudge a scalpel tip under the edge and fold it back, avoiding cutting at the cover‑glass edge. Do not use fingernail polish or ethanol on DPX.

steps.title: Handle immersion fluids after imaging
steps.instruction: Since many high‑magnification immersion fluids contain non‑polar organic compounds that dissolve DPX, clean any immersion fluid off the slide after viewing; avoid using DPX‑dissolving fluids on the slide.

steps.title: Store DPX‑mounted slides
steps.instruction: Store slides at room temperature protected from light; do not refrigerate or freeze.

steps.title: Prepare fresh PLL as needed
steps.instruction: Make fresh PLL according to the FlyLight recipe; store solution 3–6 months at 4 °C (discard if turbid) and keep lyophilized powder at –20 °C.

steps.title: Safety precautions
steps.instruction: Perform all steps involving xylene and uncured DPX in a fume hood, wear gloves, and follow appropriate hazardous‑chemical safety practices. Be self‑informed on the risks of handling xylene and DPX.
